---
title: Threads and messages
description: "Talking to a Pi Durable Platform agent from your app: listing agents, starting, listing, paging and searching threads, reading a conversation page by page, sending and steering messages, stopping, renaming, deleting and hibernating."
---

A conversation with a Pi Durable Platform agent is a **thread**. You start one, send messages to it and follow it as **server-sent events** ([Event streams](/docs/build/events)). Messages are accepted at once (`202`); the reply arrives on the thread.

## Find the agent

```sh
GET /v1/agents                      # every agent of the caller's teams (a service account's own team)
GET /v1/teams/{team}/agents         # one team's
GET /v1/agents/{agentId}            # one
```

Each agent has its `teamId`, `teamSlug` and `teamName`, its template and version, its model, `serviceManaged`, `enabled`, and `running` (whether its runtime is up now). `GET /v1/agents?includeManaged=true` also lists service-managed agents to a team's owners and admins, who can see but not use them; don't pass it with a person's token.

## Start a thread

Ask the platform for a thread, and it chooses the ID:

```sh
curl -X POST https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"visibility": "private", "title": "Release questions"}'
```

Both fields are optional, and so is the body. The answer is `201` with the thread and a `Location` header with its path. The ID is random and unguessable: use it as `{threadId}` below, and send the first message to `…/threads/{threadId}/messages`.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `visibility` | `shared` (the default) or `private`. It is fixed from now on: see [Private threads](/docs/build/private-threads) |
| `title` | Up to 200 characters. The default is "New chat", which the first message's first line replaces while it is still the default |

Anyone who may use the agent may start a thread, as for sending a message. An agent that is turned off answers `409 agent_disabled`. Until its first message, a thread is listed and announced to its creator only (anyone who may use the agent can still use a shared one by its ID). A thread that nobody sends to is removed after 30 days.

**Use this rather than choosing IDs yourself.** Thread IDs are per agent, and a platform-chosen ID can't be guessed, so nobody else can start the thread or join it before you.

### Choosing the ID yourself

Your app may still choose a thread's ID: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dashes or underscores. The first message under an ID that has no thread starts that thread, as before. So does setting its [MCP servers](/docs/build/thread-mcp-servers). But **whoever uses an ID first starts that thread**: if the ID is guessable, someone else who may use the agent can start it before you. For a shared thread, anyone who may use the agent and learns the ID can join it. If you do choose IDs, use random ones (a UUID without braces works).

## List, read, rename and delete

```sh
GET    /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads                 # list, most recent activity first
GET    /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads/{threadId}      # the transcript and the reply in progress
PATCH  /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads/{threadId}      # {"title": "…"}, 1 to 200 characters
DELETE /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads/{threadId}      # stop it and remove it from the list
```

A reserved thread, one that has no message yet, can be deleted too.

**Listing never wakes the agent**: the platform keeps a record of each thread. Each has `title` (by default the first line of its first message, up to 60 characters), `createdAt`, `updatedAt` (moves when a message is sent and when a reply ends), `busy`, `lastReplyAt`, `lastError` (why the last reply failed; absent when it succeeded), `visibility`, `createdBy` and `participants`. Reading a transcript, sending, stopping and deleting wake the agent.

### Page and search the list

Without parameters the list has every thread the caller may see, as before. Paging is opt-in:

```sh
curl "https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads?limit=50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
{"data": [{"threadId": "…", "title": "Release questions", …}, …], "nextCursor": "…"}
```

- `limit` is 1 to 200. The reply is one page, newest activity first, with `nextCursor` beside `data` when more threads follow. The last page has no `nextCursor`.
- Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`, with the same `q`. The cursor is opaque; a malformed one is `400 invalid_cursor`.
- `q` keeps the threads whose title contains it, ignoring case (at most 200 characters). It works with or without `limit`.

Every page follows the same visibility rules as the whole list: shared threads and the caller's own private ones.

### Read a conversation page by page

`GET …/threads/{threadId}` without parameters returns the whole transcript. A long conversation can be read backwards instead:

```sh
GET /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads/{threadId}?limit=50                    # the latest 50 messages
GET /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads/{threadId}?limit=50&before=<cursor>    # the 50 before them
```

- `limit` is 1 to 200; it is 50 when you send only `before`.
- The reply is the usual conversation view, with `earlierCursor` when earlier messages exist. Pass it as `before` for the page before. Without `earlierCursor`, you have reached the start.
- A page never starts with a tool result: it then also holds the reply that made the call.
- If the message a cursor names has left the conversation's view (the conversation was compacted or reset), the page is empty.
- The reply in progress and the running tools are always the current ones.

[Event streams](/docs/build/events) take `limit` too, so an app can open a long conversation with its latest messages and load earlier ones on request.

## Send a message

```sh
curl -X POST https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads/$THREAD/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "What changed in last week'\''s release?", "requestId": "msg-7f3a", "visibility": "private"}'
```

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `text` | Required, up to 32,000 characters. Text only: no files or images. |
| `requestId` | Idempotency key: a repeated one isn't submitted again. Send one with every message and reuse it on retries. |
| `visibility` | `shared` (default) or `private`, chosen when the thread starts: by `POST …/threads`, by its **first** message, or by setting its MCP servers. See [Private threads](/docs/build/private-threads). |
| `whenBusy` | What to do while a reply is running: `followUp` (the default) or `steer`. See [Steer a reply](#steer-a-reply). |
| `mcpServers` | The MCP servers your user enabled for this thread. See [Thread MCP servers](/docs/build/thread-mcp-servers). |

The answer is `202` with a `submissionId`. The first message to an ID with no thread starts it (a thread from `POST …/threads` already exists, and the message ends its reservation). Don't set an author: the platform sets it from your credential.

### Steer a reply

A message sent while the agent is replying does one of two things, chosen by `whenBusy`:

- **`followUp`** (the default): it waits for the reply in progress to end, then starts the next reply. Nothing is interrupted.
- **`steer`**: it joins the reply in progress. The agent sees it after its current round of tool calls (or with its answer), before it goes on, and the reply continues with it in mind. Use it for "actually, only last week" while the agent is still working.

```sh
curl -X POST https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads/$THREAD/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Only the release notes, please.", "requestId": "msg-7f3b", "whenBusy": "steer"}'
```

The transcript shows a steering message where the agent took it in: a user message after the tool results of the reply it changed, and before that reply's next answer. In a delta stream it arrives as a `message.added`. On an idle thread, both values simply start a reply.

## Stop, hibernate, turn off

```sh
POST /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads/{threadId}/stop   # stop the reply in progress
POST /v1/agents/{agentId}/hibernate                 # stop the runtime now; the next request wakes it
```

A stopped reply isn't an error. An agent that is turned off (`enabled: false`) refuses messages and reads with `409 agent_disabled`.

## Waking and failures

The first request to a hibernated agent starts its runtime, which takes a few seconds. While it starts, requests wait.

- `503 agent_unavailable`: the agent couldn't be started in time. Retry with backoff.
- `409 too_many_running`: a personal workspace is at its `maxRunning`. Close streams or wait for an agent to hibernate.
- `409 agent_model_unavailable`: the agent's model was turned off or unpublished; someone must choose another.
- A reply that fails shows in the transcript (an assistant message with `error`) and in the thread's `lastError`, for example when the model provider refuses the request. A message the agent couldn't answer at all also sets `lastError`, starting "No reply:".

See [Errors and limits](/docs/build/errors-and-limits).
